elections.outcome: Begin formed a coalition of Likud, the National Religious Party and Agudat Yisrael; Dash joined four months later.
Begin formed a narrow 61-seat coalition of Likud, the National Religious Party, Tami and Agudat Yisrael.
Peres and Shamir formed a national unity government, agreeing to swap the premiership after two years.
Shamir formed another unity government with the Alignment, without rotation; after it fell in March 1990 he formed a narrow right-wing and religious government.
Rabin formed a Labor–Meretz–Shas coalition of 62 MKs, with outside support from five Arab-party MKs.
Netanyahu, elected prime minister directly by about 30,000 votes, formed a six-faction coalition of 66 MKs.
Barak, elected prime minister directly, formed a seven-faction coalition of 75 MKs.
Sharon formed a coalition of Likud, Shinui, the National Religious Party and National Union, with 68 MKs.
Olmert formed a coalition of Kadima, Labor, Shas and Gil, with 67 MKs.
Although Kadima won one more seat, a majority backed Netanyahu, who formed a six-party coalition of 74 MKs.
Netanyahu formed a four-party coalition of 68 MKs.
Netanyahu formed a five-party coalition of 61 MKs.
Netanyahu could not form a coalition, and the Knesset voted 74–45 to dissolve itself, a month after being sworn in.
Neither Netanyahu nor Gantz assembled a coalition, and the Knesset dissolved, setting a third election.
Netanyahu and Gantz formed a rotation government, approved 73–46 on May 17, 2020; Gantz was to take over in November 2021.
After Netanyahu failed, Lapid assembled an eight-party coalition with Yamina's Bennett as prime minister.
Netanyahu formed a six-party coalition of Likud, Religious Zionism, Otzma Yehudit, Noam, Shas and UTJ, approved 63–54 on Dec 29, 2022.

events.title: The 'upheaval': Likud wins
events.text: For the first time, power shifted from Mapai and its heirs, in office for 29 years, to the right-wing bloc under Menachem Begin. The Alignment fell to 32 seats; Likud won 43. The result became known as "the upheaval."

events.title: Sadat visits Jerusalem
events.text: Begin received Egyptian President Anwar Sadat on his visit to Jerusalem.

events.title: Camp David framework signed
events.text: After 11 days of talks at Camp David, Begin signed a framework for a peace treaty with Egypt. Israel agreed to withdraw from the entire Sinai Peninsula.

events.title: Peace treaty with Egypt
events.text: At the White House, Begin signed the peace treaty with Egypt, the first agreement of its kind between Israel and an Arab state.

events.title: Israel invades Lebanon
events.text: Israel invaded Lebanon, with Ariel Sharon as defense minister. Sharon lost the post after Israeli-allied Christian militia killed hundreds of Palestinians in west Beirut refugee camps that September.

events.title: Unity government with rotation
events.text: Shimon Peres of the Alignment became prime minister of a government that included Likud, with Likud's Yitzhak Shamir as foreign minister. Shamir replaced Peres as prime minister on Oct 20, 1986.

source.name: Knesset, Governments of Israel (Internet Archive copy, 2013)

events.title: First intifada begins
events.text: After an Israeli vehicle in Gaza caused a crash that killed four Palestinians, protests broke out in the Jabalia refugee camp. The uprising, the first intifada, spread to the occupied West Bank.

events.title: Madrid peace conference
events.text: A conference co-chaired by Presidents Bush and Gorbachev opened with Israeli, Egyptian, Syrian and Lebanese delegations and a joint Jordanian-Palestinian one: the first time all parties to the Arab-Israeli conflict met for direct talks.

source.name: US State Department, Office of the Historian

events.title: Oslo Accords signed
events.text: Israel and the PLO signed the first Oslo Accord, in which each side recognized the other for the first time. A second accord followed in September 1995.

events.title: Peace treaty with Jordan
events.text: At the Arava border crossing, Israel and Jordan signed a peace treaty. Jordan became the second Arab country, after Egypt, to make peace with Israel.

events.title: Rabin assassinated
events.text: Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin was shot dead by Yigal Amir, a far-right Jewish activist, at a rally of more than 100,000 people in Tel Aviv. In the Oslo talks Rabin had agreed to cede some territory won in 1967 to the PLO in exchange for peace.

events.title: First direct election of a PM
events.text: For the first time voters cast two ballots, one for the Knesset and one for prime minister. Netanyahu beat Peres by about 30,000 votes, under one percent, and sectoral parties gained seats.

events.title: Barak wins second direct election
events.text: Ehud Barak beat Netanyahu for prime minister by a convincing margin, but his One Israel list won only 26 seats. For the first time the two largest factions held fewer than half the Knesset's seats.

events.title: Israel leaves southern Lebanon
events.text: The last Israeli troops withdrew from southern Lebanon, ending an 18-year presence in the security zone. The army's stay there from June 1982 had cost 1,216 Israeli soldiers' lives.

events.title: Sharon visit; second intifada
events.text: Opposition leader Ariel Sharon visited the Temple Mount, which Muslims call the Noble Sanctuary, and violence erupted. Palestinians attribute the uprising to the visit; his supporters say it was already planned.

events.title: PM-only election: Sharon wins
events.text: In the first election ever held for prime minister alone, with no Knesset vote, Sharon beat Barak with 62.4%. Turnout, 62.3%, was the lowest in Israel's history to that point. A month later Israel returned to its former system.

events.title: Back to a single ballot
events.text: Sharon had abolished direct election of the prime minister, and Israel returned to single-ballot elections. Held during the second intifada, the vote gave his Likud 38 seats to Labor's 19.

events.title: Gaza disengagement
events.text: Sharon's government began a unilateral withdrawal from Gaza and a small part of the West Bank, reversing his decades of support for expanding settlements.

events.title: Sharon leaves Likud, founds Kadima
events.text: Facing a Likud rebellion over the Gaza pullout, Prime Minister Sharon quit Likud to lead a new centrist party, later named Kadima, into early elections.

events.title: Sharon's stroke
events.text: On the eve of a scheduled heart procedure, Sharon suffered a massive stroke and entered a coma. He was still in a coma in 2013 and died in January 2014.

events.title: Second Lebanon War
events.text: Hezbollah fighters killed three Israeli soldiers and seized two in a cross-border raid, setting off 34 days of fighting in Lebanon.

events.title: Netanyahu returns to office
events.text: The Knesset approved Netanyahu's government, Israel's 32nd, by 69–45 with five abstentions, after he assembled a coalition amid tensions within Likud.

events.title: Social protests peak
events.text: After a summer of tent protests over the high cost of living, more than 400,000 people rallied for "social justice" across Israel, in what was called the biggest protest in the country's history.

events.title: Nation-state law passes
events.text: The Knesset passed, 62–55, a Basic Law stating that the right to national self-determination in Israel is "exclusive" to the Jewish people. It downgraded Arabic from an official language to a "special status."

events.title: First of five elections fails
events.text: After the April vote, Netanyahu could not form a coalition: Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu and the Haredi parties split over the draft law. The Knesset dissolved itself 74–45, forcing an unprecedented second election that year.

events.title: Netanyahu indicted
events.text: Attorney General Avichai Mandelblit announced that Netanyahu would be charged with bribery, fraud and breach of trust in Cases 1000, 2000 and 4000. He was the first sitting Israeli prime minister accused of bribery.

events.title: Netanyahu–Gantz unity government
events.text: After a third election, the Knesset approved a Netanyahu–Gantz government 73–46. Under the deal, Benny Gantz was to become prime minister on Nov 17, 2021.

events.title: Abraham Accords signed
events.text: At the White House, Israel signed agreements with the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, which joined Egypt and Jordan as Arab states at formal peace with Israel.

events.title: Violence in mixed cities
events.text: Amid fighting in Gaza and clashes around Al-Aqsa Mosque, Jewish and Arab mobs attacked each other in Lod, Acre, Ramle and Bat Yam, the widest unrest between citizens since October 2000, when police killed 13 protesters, 12 of them Palestinian citizens of Israel.

events.title: Ra'am signs on to a coalition
events.text: Mansour Abbas signed a deal to bring Ra'am into the Bennett–Lapid coalition, the first Arab party leader in half a century to do so. The coalition pledged about NIS 53 billion for Arab communities.

events.title: Bennett–Lapid government sworn in
events.text: The Knesset approved the new government 60–59, ending Netanyahu's 12-year tenure. Naftali Bennett became prime minister.

events.title: Knesset dissolves; Lapid PM
events.text: The Knesset dissolved itself 92–0 and set the fifth election in three and a half years for Nov 1. Yair Lapid became interim prime minister at midnight.

events.title: Netanyahu bloc wins 64 seats
events.text: The two blocs were nearly tied in votes, but Meretz and Balad fell below the threshold. Likud and its allies won 64 seats, enough for Netanyahu to form a "pure" right-wing government.

events.title: Judicial overhaul unveiled
events.text: Justice Minister Yariv Levin proposed barring the courts' "reasonableness" review, giving the government effective control of judicial appointments, and letting 61 MKs re-enact laws the court strikes down.

events.title: Overhaul paused after strike
events.text: After mass protests and a nationwide strike, Netanyahu delayed the overhaul: "When there's an opportunity to avoid civil war through dialogue, I, as prime minister, am taking a time out for dialogue."

events.title: 'Reasonableness' law passes
events.text: The Knesset passed 64–0 a law limiting the courts' review of government decisions for "reasonableness." The opposition boycotted the vote.

events.title: Hamas-led attack on Israel
events.text: Thousands of Hamas-led gunmen stormed southern Israel, killing some 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages to Gaza, which started the war in Gaza.

events.title: First truce and hostage releases
events.text: A seven-day truce began. Hamas freed 105 hostages, 81 of them Israelis, and Israel released 210 Palestinian prisoners, all women or minors. Fighting resumed on Dec 1.

events.title: Court voids reasonableness law
events.text: Eight of 15 Supreme Court justices voted to strike down the reasonableness amendment, the first time the court nullified a Basic Law or an amendment to one. Twelve ruled that it had that power.

events.title: Court orders Haredi draft
events.text: A unanimous nine-justice panel ruled there is "no legal basis for avoiding the recruitment of yeshiva students" and that the state may not keep funding yeshivas for students eligible for service.

events.title: Gaza ceasefire takes effect
events.text: A ceasefire began and Hamas freed its first three hostages under a deal whose first phase was to last 42 days.

events.title: War resumes; Ben-Gvir returns
events.text: Israel launched its deadliest strikes on Gaza since the January ceasefire. Hours later, Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit, which had resigned in January in protest at the ceasefire, announced it would rejoin.

events.title: Twelve-day war with Iran
events.text: Israel bombed Iranian nuclear sites at Natanz and Isfahan, and Iran retaliated with drones and missiles. President Trump announced a ceasefire, calling it "the 12 Day War."

events.title: UTJ quits the coalition
events.text: Both factions of United Torah Judaism, Degel Hatorah and Agudat Yisrael, left the government and coalition in protest over the draft bill, cutting the coalition from 68 seats to 61.

events.title: Shas quits the government
events.text: Shas announced its resignation from the government amid the coalition's failure to advance a bill on military service for Haredi men, but said it would not vote to bring down Netanyahu's coalition.

events.title: Last living hostages come home
events.text: Under a ceasefire deal brokered by President Trump, Hamas released the 20 remaining living hostages and Israel released nearly 2,000 Palestinian prisoners. That day Hamas handed over 4 of the 28 dead hostages' bodies.

events.title: US and Israel strike Iran
events.text: The United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran two days after US–Iran nuclear talks in Geneva ended without a breakthrough. Iran responded with missile and air strikes across the region, including on Israel.

events.title: Knesset dissolves; vote set
events.text: The 25th Knesset dissolved itself 62–0 overnight and set the election for Oct 27, 2026. A separate vote kept mandatory military service at 32 months.

events.title: Court reinstates Arab lists
events.text: The Supreme Court unanimously overturned the Central Elections Committee's disqualification of the Joint List and Ra'am. Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh withdrew after the court signaled a majority favored barring him.
